observation.visible_scene: A close, slightly high-angle view of a flat black metal griddle/plancha resting on a gas stovetop. The left half of the cooking surface is coated with a dull oil/liquid sheen bounded by an irregular edge, while the right side is drier and darker; a bright white window-like reflection sits along the far-right edge of the glossy surface. Below the front rim of the griddle the stove's metal grate bars and round burner caps are visible.
visible_changes: The gas flame beneath the left burner flickers on and off repeatedly through the segment: blue flame is absent in the early frames, appears around t≈1.5–2.0 s, fades, reappears briefly near t≈2.5 s and t≈3.1 s, and is gone in the final frames. This is an intermittent flickering of an already-burning flame, not a single ignition or extinguishing.

The boundary of the oil sheen on the left surface shifts and undulates slightly over time (the wet region edges creep a little to the right at the top), consistent with a thin liquid film moving/spreading on the heated plate rather than a new pour.

The white reflection on the right edge and the position of the griddle, grate bars, and burner caps remain essentially fixed, indicating no object translation and no significant camera motion; only minor frame-to-frame jitter is present.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the flame flicker is caused by airflow, a regulator setting, or evaporation of the oil; whether the griddle is being preheated for cooking; what occurs before t=0 and after the last frame.
uncertain_details: Exact cause and direction of the small oil-boundary movement (spreading vs. evaporation) cannot be determined from these frames alone.
Whether any slight apparent shift of the whole scene is camera micro-jitter or true motion is not resolvable given the static background.
